headline: Keep only candidates that can still become maximum
statement: For every contiguous window of k values in nums, return its maximum in left-to-right window order. Use O(n) time.
intuition: Keep possible maximum positions in a queue whose values decrease from front to back. A newer value can replace older candidates that are no larger, because it will remain in the window longer. Remove positions that have left the window. The front then gives the maximum.
approach: Remove expired indices from the front.
Remove back indices whose values are at most the new value.
Once a complete window exists, emit the front's value.
correctness: The deque contains current-window candidates in decreasing value order. Any removed back candidate has a newer value no smaller, so it cannot become the maximum before it expires. Expired front indices are invalid. Thus the front is the largest value among all relevant candidates and the true maximum.
bruteForce: Scan all k values in every window, giving O(nk) time.

complexity.explanation: Each index enters once and leaves at most once from either end.

pitfalls: Store indices so expiry can be tested.
Remove indices at or before i-k.
Repeated values are safe to discard from the back because the newer copy expires later.
